cards.explanation: The answer is day. The landowner agrees to pay the early crew a denarius for the day (Matthew 20:2). Notice the pay is named up front. Hold on to that agreement, friends, because it matters later.

The answer is "I will pay you whatever is right." He says, "…I will pay you whatever is right." (Matthew 20:4) Notice he doesn't name a number this time. So they go in with only that promise (Matthew 20:5). Keep that in mind when the evening comes.

The answer is True! The text says he went out again about the sixth hour and the ninth hour and did the same thing (Matthew 20:5). Same man, same marketplace, same invitation. This guy has a hiring routine, and I respect it.

The answer is hired. They say, "Because no one has hired us…" (Matthew 20:7) That's the reason they give for standing around. And I know something about waiting for somebody to come open the junk drawer I got stuck in.
The answer is True. He tells them, "You also go into my vineyard…" (Matthew 20:7) The day is almost over and he still sends them in. I think those workers were mighty surprised to hear it.

The answer is last hired to first hired. The owner says to pay them "…starting with the last ones hired and moving on to the first." (Matthew 20:8) So the late crew is first in line for the money. The first hired come last.

The answer is a full denarius, each one. The text says the workers hired about the eleventh hour "…each received a denarius." (Matthew 20:9) An hour of work and a whole day's pay. I'd be checking the envelope twice.

The answer is False. The early workers assumed they would receive more, but "…each of them also received a denarius." (Matthew 20:10) That's the same pay as the late crew, and the same as the deal they agreed on (Matthew 20:2).

The words are grumble and landowner. The text says "…they began to grumble against the landowner." (Matthew 20:11) They did it on receiving their pay, and I think we've all grumbled over a paycheck at some point. The landowner is the man who made the deal with them (Matthew 20:2), so the grumbling is aimed at him.

The answer is that he agreed to one denarius. The landowner calls him "Friend" first, then asks, "Did you not agree with me on one denarius?" (Matthew 20:13) The deal was made at the start, friends, and the pay matched it.

The answer is "Are you envious because I am generous." The landowner asks, "Or are you envious because I am generous?" (Matthew 20:15) It lands right on the heart of the matter. The landowner says he is generous, and he gets to be.
